result_text:
**Northgate Clinic profile, January–June 2026**

The account appears under two IDs, and its billing is patchy. I could only partly resolve the gaps from the data.

**Identity**
- **ACC-1042, Northgate Clinic:** valid 2025-01-01 to 2026-03-31.
- **ACC-1077, Northgate Health Partners (formerly Northgate Clinic):** valid from 2026-04-01.
- I treated these as one entity. The only link is the "formerly Northgate Clinic" text in the account name. There is no ID-to-ID mapping, so that link is worth confirming.

**Billing**

| Month | Account | Plan | Volume | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Jan | ACC-1042 | standard | 1,840 | $772.80 |
| Feb | none | | | |
| Mar | ACC-1042 | enterprise-annual | 1,910 | $592.10 |
| Apr | ACC-1077 | enterprise-annual | 1,120 | $347.20 |
| May | ACC-1077 | enterprise-annual | 1,085 | $336.35 |
| Jun | none | | | |

The implied rate is $0.42 per unit on standard and $0.31 per unit on enterprise-annual, in every row.

**Dated changes**
- **February:** the contract status for ACC-1042 is "paused". It is "active" in January and March.
- **2026-03-01:** the plan changed from standard to enterprise-annual (ACC-1042).
- **2026-03-31:** ACC-1042's validity ends.
- **2026-04-01:** ACC-1077 begins. It has no plan-change row of its own and is billed on enterprise-annual from April. Its contract status is active in April and May.
- **Billed volume:** it went from 1,910 in March to 1,120 in April and 1,085 in May.

**Tickets (6 in total)**

| Account | Date | Category |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACC-1042 | 01-08 | feature-request |
| ACC-1042 | 03-11 | feature-request |
| ACC-1042 | 03-26 | integration |
| ACC-1077 | 04-01 | billing-question |
| ACC-1077 | 04-04 | billing-question |
| ACC-1077 | 05-25 | outage-report |

There are none in June.

**Gaps and caveats**
- **February billing:** there is no row. The "paused" status is consistent with that, but it doesn't prove no bill was issued.
- **June billing:** there is no ACC-1077 row, and the cause is unknown. It could be that no bill was issued or that the export is incomplete. The other three accounts all have June billing. The contract-status file stops at May for every account, so it can't help.
- **Volume drop:** the fall from March to April coincides with the account ID change. I haven't tested whether the two are related, and I'm not attributing it to anything.
- **Billing questions:** two billing-question tickets were opened on ACC-1077 in its first four days. I'm not attributing those to anything either.

If you want the volume drop or the June gap settled, those would go to hypothesis-driven analysis. The June gap is better answered by asking the data owner for the June export. No holdout data is left, so confirming the volume drop would need future or independent data.
